result:
The proposed answer, t = q^{2h}, fails already in the case h = 1, so I reject it.

For h = 1 the problem becomes a question about points in PG(3,q) where every plane contains at most t points and the size is (t−2)q + t.

- An ovoid has q²+1 points, and every plane meets it in at most q+1 points. Taking t = q+1 gives (q−1)q + q + 1 = q²+1, so the bound is attained at t = q+1.
- With t = q², the bound would be (q²−2)q + q² = q³+q²−2q. A set of that size with at most q² points on every plane is not possible, since the complement of a plane has only q³ points, so the bound is not attained there.

So the claimed general pattern t = q^{(k−2)h} does not hold at h = 1. The correct value should reduce to q+1 when h = 1. One candidate is t = q^{h−1}(q+1), but I am recalling that from memory and have not derived it. The proposed answer is wrong either way.

VERDICT: REJECT
